$comment: Style-gate routes manifest (Phase 1 of the CI style-gating plan).
One entry per route the headless capture renders. The capture spec
(style-capture.spec.ts) produces, per route, a UI-Bridge snapshot JSON
(.artifacts/snapshots/<id>.json) and a deterministic PNG screenshot
(.artifacts/frames/<id>.png); a later phase feeds both to the
vision-audit analyzer bin.
TWO CAPTURE LANES. The `public` field selects which snapshot mechanism a
route is captured with -- see capturePathFor() in manifest.ts, the one
place the field is interpreted:
public: false -> RELAY lane. Rendered WITH the setup-minted storageState
and snapshotted through the same-origin relay proxy
(/api/ui-bridge/control/snapshot), which is served by the in-page
CommandRelayListener. That listener returns null without a resolved
{userId, sessionId} (provider.tsx commandRelayRegistrationMetadata), so
this lane REQUIRES an authenticated tab -- an unauthenticated route on
this lane would always 503 NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED.
public: true -> INJECTED lane (relay-independent). Rendered in a FRESH,
UNAUTHENTICATED browser context -- no storageState, no auth/consent
seeding, no login-surface guard -- and snapshotted IN-PAGE from UI
Bridge's shipped injected runtime: the
@qontinui/ui-bridge/injected/bundle.global.js IIFE added as a
pre-first-paint init script, then
window.__uiBridgeInjected.execute('getControlSnapshot', {}). This is the
same mechanism ui-bridge-inject and @qontinui/ui-bridge-wrapper's
InjectedTransport use to drive pages that ship ZERO UI Bridge code. No
relay, no listener, no session -- so a signed-out surface IS capturable.
(An earlier revision of this comment said `public` was RESERVED and
unsupported; that was true only until the injected lane landed.)
Both lanes emit the SAME artifact shapes through the same normalizer, so
the downstream analyzer cannot tell them apart.
SCORING IS SEPARATE FROM CAPTURE. .github/workflows/style-gate.yml scores a
HARDCODED route list (ROUTES="co-pilot build-workflows library"), so a
route added here is CAPTURED and uploaded but not yet scored. Adding it to
that list also requires specs/<id>.json -- a missing spec is an INFRA error
that reds the job in BOTH shadow and enforce. Ship the spec first.
Fields:
id          filesystem-safe slug, also the artifact basename.
path        route path passed to page.goto().
public      REQUIRED boolean. Selects the capture lane (above):
false -> relay lane, rendered WITH the setup-minted
storageState (style-gate project).
true  -> injected lane, rendered in a fresh unauthenticated
context with the UI-Bridge injected runtime. A non-boolean
value is a loud manifest error, never a default.
settleMs    extra wait after networkidle before capture. RETAINED but
currently unused by BOTH lanes -- readiness is signal-driven,
not timer-driven (relay lane: relay-attach + app-shell
sidebar; injected lane: the runtime's own settle gate). A
fixed wait is exactly as flaky under variable CI load.
description human note on what the route is.
Deliberately SMALL high-value seed set. The set EXPANDS after burn-in once
the capture+baseline loop is proven stable in CI. Add routes by appending
objects here -- no code change required.

routes.description: Authenticated Home landing (src/app/(app)/co-pilot/page.tsx). An authed visit to / forwards here (use-landing-page.ts) -- this IS the post-login Home surface. RESOLVED FLAKE (was CAPTURE-UNAVAILABLE): the 503 NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED was NOT co-pilot-page-specific -- it was a COLD-START race on whichever route renders FIRST (co-pilot is first here; workers=1, serial). A fresh `npm run dev` server compiles the (app) layout/providers + this route + the /api/ui-bridge/control/snapshot relay-proxy route ON FIRST HIT, the client-side auth context keeps the (app) layout's SHARED AuthLoadingShell ('Loading...') up -- WITHHOLDING the UI-Bridge provider subtree incl. CommandRelayListener -- until the cold auth round-trip resolves, and only THEN can the relay attach. That cold compile+auth+attach sum exceeds the 60s per-test budget, so co-pilot's failure-time snapshot showed the shared AuthLoadingShell still up at 60s while the warm routes after it captured in ~20s. Proven via run 27000271391 artifacts: co-pilot diag usersMe=200 / looksLikeLogin=false (auth fine), snapshot = 'img + Loading...' (the shared shell), 1.0m timeout in captureSnapshot; build-workflows 20.8s + library 15.9s green. The EARLIER fix's per-test waitForAuthedShell (45s, silently swallowed) made it worse by eating the budget waiting for a shell that never cleared, and its beforeAll warmup only waited for the shell (also swallowed) so it never drove the relay to attach. The CURRENT fix makes beforeAll run the FULL readiness dance (navigate -> shell clears -> co-pilot ready badge -> RELAY ATTACHES) and BLOCKS on the relay actually attaching, in the no-per-test-cap hook (180s) -- so the cold compile+auth+attach happen ONCE before any per-test budget, leaving the first real test as warm as the others. Per-test waitForAuthedShell is now a short 20s (the warm path clears fast) so the bulk of the 60s budget is left for the relay poll, and co-pilot additionally waits for its own CoPilotReadyStatus badge (co-pilot-specific readiness). settleMs stays the standard 3000 -- readiness is signal-driven, not timer-driven.
Authenticated workflow builder (src/app/(app)/build/workflows/page.tsx). /dashboard redirect-shim resolves here in ai product-mode (dashboard/page.tsx).
Authenticated Library landing (src/app/(app)/library/page.tsx). Self-contained category-card grid -- no RequireProject gate, so it renders a stable content surface regardless of selected project.

PUBLIC seed route -- the sign-in surface (src/app/(marketing)/login/page.tsx), the first route captured through the INJECTED lane. What it proves: a route with NO authenticated user is now capturable. The relay lane cannot reach it BY CONSTRUCTION (no {userId, sessionId} -> no CommandRelayListener -> 503 NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED, which is exactly why every other seed route is authed), so a non-empty snapshot for this id is proof the capture came from the relay-INDEPENDENT in-page injected runtime and not from the proxy. It is also the highest-value public surface to gate later: it is the one page every signed-out visitor sees, and the P0 the relay lane guards against (assertNotLoginSurface) is precisely an authed route silently rendering THIS one -- so a committed baseline of what /login is SUPPOSED to look like is the natural complement to that guard. NOT yet in the workflow's scored ROUTES list: adding it there needs specs/login.json first (a missing spec is an INFRA error in both shadow and enforce). Captured + uploaded meanwhile, which is what the burn-in needs.
